hot.title: A Comparison of Responses from Human Therapists and Large Language Model–Based Chatbots to Assess Therapeutic Communication: Mixed Methods Study
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Consumers are increasingly using large language model-based chatbots to seek mental health advice or intervention due to ease of access and limited availability of mental health professionals. However, their suitability and safety for mental health applications remain underexplored, particularly in comparison to professional therapeutic practices. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate how general-purpose chatbots respond to mental health scenarios and compare their responses to those provided by licensed therapists. Specifically, we sought to identify chatbots' strengths and limitations, as well as the ethical and practical considerations necessary for their use in mental health care. METHODS: We conducted a mixed methods study to compare responses from chatbots and licensed therapists to scripted mental health scenarios. We created 2 fictional scenarios and prompted 3 chatbots to create 6 interaction logs. We recruited 17 therapists and conducted study sessions that consisted of 3 activities. First, therapists responded to the 2 scenarios using a Qualtrics form. Second, therapists went through the 6 interaction logs using a think-aloud procedure to highlight their thoughts about the chatbots' responses. Finally, we conducted a semistructured interview to explore subjective opinions on the use of chatbots for supporting mental health. The study sessions were analyzed using thematic analysis. The interaction logs from chatbot and therapist responses were coded using the Multitheoretical List of Therapeutic Interventions codes and then compared to each other. RESULTS: We identified 7 themes describing the strengths and limitations of the chatbots as compared to therapists. hot.title: Strategic human resource management in the digital economy era: an empirical study of challenges and opportunities among MSMEs and startups in Indonesia
hot.abstract: This study investigates the impact of digital Human Resource Management (HRM) strategies on workforce productivity and organizational performance within Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and startups in Indonesia. Anchored in the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the research conceptualizes digital HRM as a strategic asset that enhances organizational performance by enabling firms to develop, deploy, and reconfigure human capital capabilities in response to digital transformation. The conceptual model includes five constructs: Digital Technology Adoption in HRM, Digital Training and Development, Work Flexibility and Hybrid Management, Innovation in Recruitment and Retention, and Utilization of HR Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Data were collected through structured questionnaires distributed to MSME and startup leaders and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with Smart PLS. The results indicate that Digital Technology Adoption, Digital Training and Development, and Work Flexibility do not significantly influence workforce productivity or organizational performance (p > 0.05). However, Innovation in Recruitment and Retention and the Utilization of HR Analytics and AI have a significant and positive impact on both workforce productivity and performance outcomes (p = 0.000). These findings highlight that while not all digital HR strategies yield immediate benefits, the ability to build dynamic capabilities through innovative talent practices and data-driven HR systems is essential to achieving competitive advantage and organizational success in the digital economy.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Customer data access and fintech entry: Early evidence from open banking
hot.abstract: Open banking (OB) empowers bank customers to share their financial transaction data with fintechs and other banks. New cross-country data shows 49 countries adopted OB policies, privacy preferences predict policy adoption, and adoption spurs fintech entry. UK microdata shows that OB enables: (i) consumers to access both financial advice and credit; (ii) SMEs to establish new lending relationships. In a calibrated model, OB universally improves welfare through entry and product improvements when used for advice. When used for credit, OB promotes entry and competition by reducing adverse selection, but higher prices for costlier or privacy-conscious consumers partially offset these benefits.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences. This study examined the multidimensional impact of influencer marketing by analyzing engagement metrics, marketing effectiveness, and consumer decision-making processes, based on consumers in the Greek sector. Through a structured methodological framework, the research employed a questionnaire-based survey, statistical modeling, and Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) scenarios to assess consumer interactions with influencer-driven content. Findings highlight that while influencer marketing enhances brand engagement and sales, its effectiveness varies based on content authenticity, transparency, and user trust. Additionally, consumer purchasing decisions are influenced by social media visibility, personalized marketing strategies, and digital platform usability. This study underscores the need for strategic influencer selection and information-driven marketing optimization to sustain long-term consumer engagement. These insights provide practical implications for businesses aiming to enhance digital marketing strategies and contribute to the ongoing discourse on social commerce and consumer-centric marketing models.

hot.title: AI-Driven Financial Transparency and Corporate Governance: Enhancing Accounting Practices with Evidence from Jordan
hot.abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into financial transparency and corporate governance has reshaped how organizations ensure accountability, regulatory compliance, and risk management. This study examines the impact of AI-driven financial transparency on corporate governance and regulatory reform, focusing on Jordan. Utilizing a stratified random sampling approach, data were collected from 564 corporate professionals across key economic sectors. Statistical analyses, including structural equation modeling (SEM) and multiple regression analysis, reveal that AI adoption significantly enhances corporate governance effectiveness (R2 = 0.582), improves risk management (R2 = 0.502), and increases stakeholder engagement (R2 = 0.681). AI also facilitates regulatory compliance by automating monitoring processes and reducing human errors in financial disclosures. However, challenges such as bias in AI algorithms, data privacy concerns, and the need for regulatory adaptation persist. These findings contribute to the body of knowledge on AI-driven governance and provide insights for policymakers and corporate leaders.

hot.title: Effect of anthropomorphism and perceived intelligence in chatbot avatars of visual design on user experience: accounting for perceived empathy and trust
hot.abstract: Introduction The rapid advancement of intelligent chatbots has transformed human-AI interaction, offering novel opportunities to enhance user experience (UX) through psychological and design interventions. However, the mechanisms by which chatbot design features influence UX remain understudied, particularly regarding the roles of emotional and cognitive mediators. Methods This study employed a 2 × 2 within-subjects experimental design with 160 participants to investigate the effects of anthropomorphism (high vs. low) and perceived intelligence (high vs. low) in chatbot avatars on UX. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was utilized to analyze the mediating roles of perceived empathy and trust in this relationship. Results Direct effects of anthropomorphism and perceived intelligence on UX were nonsignificant. However, their combined influence was significantly mediated by perceived empathy and trust ( β = 0.48, * p * < 0.01). Specifically, highly anthropomorphic avatars correlated with elevated empathy ( β = 0.32) and trust ( β = 0.27), which in turn improved UX. Discussion These findings underscore the importance of emotional engagement over mere intelligence in designing effective chatbots. This research contributes unique insights into the complex mechanisms governing user interactions with intelligent chatbots, emphasizing the need for design strategies that prioritize emotional connections and cognitive ease.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Marketing Within the Framework of Sustainable Management
hot.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not only revolutionizing digital marketing through personalized customer experiences and optimized advertising strategies, but it is also contributing to sustainability initiatives. As AI reshapes digital marketing, its impact on sustainability is becoming increasingly significant. This dynamic highlights the necessity of exploring how AI can be utilized to foster more sustainable marketing practices. This study seeks to answer the pivotal question: “How does AI impact the sustainability of digital marketing?” A systematic literature review was conducted in this study, following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) framework to identify various relevant articles in the areas of sustainability and marketing. Furthermore, this study examines the crucial role of AI in enhancing sustainable business practices, highlighting a significant increase in adoption among enterprises. The findings demonstrate that the effective integration of AI into digital marketing enhances environmental sustainability, supports the attainment of economic sustainability objectives, and contributes positively to social sustainability outcomes. This study contributes to the field by providing a comprehensive analysis of the intersection between AI and sustainable marketing practices and offers valuable insights for marketers, businesses, and policymakers.

hot.title: The multinational enterprise, capabilities, and digitalization: governance and growth with world disorder
hot.abstract: Abstract This essay revisits my 2014 JIBS article about the potential for integrating international business internalization theory with a strategic management capabilities perspective. It recaps the capabilities framework with an emphasis on the learning required of emerging market multinationals and illustrates this with the case of Hyundai Motor Company’s internationalization and growth. It also discusses two aspects of the global economy that have become more prominent since 2014 in shaping international business: geopolitical uncertainty and digitalization. A rise in geopolitical tensions appears to be rebalancing the relationships between multinationals and home/host governments. Digitalization facilitates international business; but it adds new vulnerabilities by (further) accelerating competition, enabling new rivals, and introducing systemic risks into digital supply chains. Implications for managers, board members, and international business scholars are drawn.

latest.title: Family environment, health risk behaviors, and mental health among chinese five-year vocational education students: a cross-sectional network analysis
latest.abstract: Abstract Background Adolescent mental health problems, particularly depression and anxiety, pose a global public health challenge. Family environment and health risk behaviors are key influencing factors, yet their complex interrelationships with psychological symptoms remain unclear. This study employed network analysis to investigate these associations, aiming to identify core symptoms and potential gender differences. Methods A total of 1,601 students were recruited from two higher vocational colleges in Nanning, Guangxi, using a cluster random sampling method. Adolescents' family environment, health risk behaviors, and mental health status were assessed using the Family Environment Scale, the Student Health Status and Influencing Factors Questionnaire, and the Mental Health Scale for Middle School Students, respectively. The EBICglasso method was used to estimate networks and derive centrality indices, followed by the Network Comparison Test to evaluate gender differences. Results "Depression" and "Anxiety" exhibited the highest strength centrality as core symptoms. Family "Cohesion" and "Conflict" served as key bridge nodes connecting health risk behaviors to mental health. The strongest association was observed between "Sleep deprivation" and "Depression." No significant gender differences were found in network structure. Conclusion Depression and anxiety are central to adolescent mental health problems, with family cohesion and sleep deprivation representing important intervention targets. Family-based emotional communication training and sleep health promotion may hold preventive value.

latest.title: Analisis Kredibilitas Konten Instagram Terhadap Kepercayaan Calon Jamaah Milenial dalam Perumusan Strategi Konten (Studi Kasus PT An-Nahl Umrah dan Haji)
latest.abstract: Increasing number of Umrah and Hajj pilgrims, where the tight competition among travel agencies in the digital era, and the rise of travel agency fraud cases through social media have created a crisis in the level of trust of prospective pilgrims, especially millennials as active Instagram users. This study aims to analyze the influence of the credibility of Instagram content on the trust of prospective millennial pilgrims in order to provide content strategy recommendations for PT An-Nahl Umrah and Hajj. This study uses a quantitative approach with a survey method. The sampling technique in this study use purposive sampling with 75 respondents. Data were collected through a Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using validity, reliability, classical assumptions and multiple linear regression through the SPSS 26 program. The analysis shows that simultaneously, the three indicators have significant influence on trust, with an F value of 34.193, and partially only the trustworthiness indicator has a dominant influence on trust of β = 0.598, while expertise and attractiveness partially do not have a significant influence on trust. From the results of this study it can be concluded that transparency, honesty and accuracy of information such as testimonial content are the main factors in building trust among prospective millennial pilgrims.

latest.title: The Influence of Collectivist Culture on Senior High School Students’ Cognition of Cyberbullying
latest.abstract: Cyberbullying has been an emerging problem among high schoolers and is increasing in rate with the wide use of the internet, and its negative effect on individual mental health. In this study, the researcher aims to explore the impact of collectivist culture to the high school students’ perception of cyberbullying by using a survey that led to 324 valid respondents. The findings show that the collectivist cultural values have a significant effect on High School students as most students consider cyberbullying as an irrational emotional release, anti-social and legally outlawed. In this type of culture, pursuing group harmony may be a cultural incentive for not challenging and confronting others openly, but students still consider that online aggression does result in harm. Based on the research results, this study recommends two policies: First, the need to increase the education of students’ cultural literacy so that students can harmonize with their groups and also be responsible as individuals in dealing with cyberbullying; and secondly, strengthening the reporting system and supporting students in school to be able to report so as to minimize refusal in action in the event of cyberbullying to prevent students from being silenced by peer pressure that can lead to dangerous responses. Studies like this one inform theoretical frameworks for intervening in the context of school bullying and give practical suggestions for culturally-responsive intervention strategies in collectivist contexts.

latest.title: The association between dietary changes for weight loss and the mental health status of American adults
latest.abstract: Background Weight loss provides numerous physical health benefits. However, prior research has mainly examined the mental health effects of weight loss strategies in the general population, rather than on individuals actively trying to lose weight. Aim We explored the link between dietary changes for weight loss and mental health, focusing on depression severity measured by the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 and the number of days mental health was not good. Methods We analyzed data from 3975 participants in the 2005–2006 U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, using ordinary least squares regression and binomial regression. Results Skipping meals ( B = 0.80, p < .001) and female ( B = 0.82, p < .001) were associated with higher PHQ-9 scores. Conversely, older age ( B = −0.001, p < .001), having college degrees or above ( B = −0.59, p < .01), Mexican American ( B = −0.43, p < .01), and higher income ( B = −0.20, p < .001) correlated with lower PHQ-9 scores. For predicting days mental health was not good, females had higher odds (OR = 1.54, p < .001) while older age (OR = 0.99, p < .01), Mexican American (OR = 0.68, p < .01), college degrees or above (OR = 0.71, p < .05), and higher income (OR = 0.93, p < .001) had lower odds. Conclusion Healthcare professionals providing weight loss guidance should consider patients’ baseline mental health and changes associated with different dietary strategies. Using longitudinal methods to establish causal links between diet and mental health is recommended.

latest.title: Strategic CSR in family firms
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how family ownership influences corporate social responsibility (CSR) using a comprehensive sample of US firms. Design/methodology/approach Using 24,531 firm-year observations from 1992 to 2019, we employ firm fixed effects and propensity score matching to compare CSR performance between family and non-family firms. Findings We find that family firms exhibit significantly higher overall CSR performance than non-family firms. Economically, family ownership is associated with an increase of approximately 0.13 CSR points, representing about 45% of the sample mean CSR score. Importantly, this difference is driven primarily by family firms’ stronger emphasis on averting CSR-related concerns rather than greater engagement in positive CSR initiatives. Further analyses show that family firms match or outperform non-family firms across all CSR dimensions, particularly in areas linked to long-term business sustainability. We also find that CSR engagement increases following family CEO successions but declines after professional successions, consistent with a strategic use of CSR to support long-term survival. Originality/value This study provides comprehensive evidence that family ownership is positively associated with CSR performance and highlights the role of CEO succession in shaping CSR engagement, offering new insights into the strategic role of CSR in family firms’ long-term survival.

latest.title: Associations between types of screen use and bedtimes among a large sample of adolescents: age and typical bedtime variations from the COMPASS study
latest.abstract: Abstract Background Recreational screen time is linked to poorer sleep among adolescents. However, most evidence focuses on total recreational screen time rather than on time spent on different screen-based activities. Also, few studies have specifically examined bedtime, an actionable determinant of adolescent sleep hygiene. To date, it is not clear how age and typical bedtime influence this relationship. The objective of this study was to examine the associations between time spent on different screen-based activities and adolescents’ bedtimes. We also aimed to examine how these associations vary based on age and typical bedtime. Methods Using a cross-sectional design, we analyzed data collected from 67,710 adolescents aged 11 to 19 (age: 14.4 (± 1.5) ; females: 51.2%) attending 154 Quebec schools in 2025 as part of the COMPASS study. Quantile regressions were conducted to assess associations between the time adolescents spent on different screen-based activities (i.e., browsing/scrolling social media, playing video games, sending messages, surfing the Internet, watching/streaming television shows or movies) and their bedtimes. The analyses were stratified by age and typical bedtime and adjusted for the adolescents’ sex and family-level material affluence. A difference-in-difference analysis was also conducted. Results Each type of recreational screen activity was positively associated with later bedtimes. Compared with adolescents who used screens ≤ 1 h per day, those reporting more than 3 h of screen use had bedtimes occurring approximately 45 min later for social media use, video gaming, and messaging, and about 30 min later for Internet surfing and television viewing. The difference in bedtime associated with higher versus lower screen use (≤ 1 h vs. > 3 h/day) wa

latest.title: Insomnia versus daytime sleepiness: distinct behavioural phenotypes of mood and binge eating in adults with clinical obesity
latest.abstract: Abstract Background/Objectives. Insomnia and excessive daytime sleepiness are common in adults with obesity but typically examined in isolation. We tested whether, jointly, they identify behavioural phenotypes with distinct eating and mood profiles. Subjects/Methods. Cross-sectional analysis of 2,016 adults from the Montpellier Obesity Care Cohort (MOCC) (76% women; mean BMI 37.1 kg/m²). Participants completed the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Binge Eating Scale (BES), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), Perceived Stress Scale, and Intuitive Eating Scale-2 (IES-2). Four phenotypes were defined a priori using ISI ≥ 15 and ESS ≥ 11: good sleeper, isolated insomnia, isolated sleepiness, combined. Multivariable regressions were adjusted for age, sex and BMI. Results. Phenotype distribution was 53.6% good sleeper, 18.2% isolated insomnia, 13.8% isolated sleepiness, 14.4% combined. ISI and ESS were only moderately correlated (ρ = 0.30). Isolated insomnia was most strongly associated with anxiety (HAD-A ≥ 11: adjusted OR [aOR] 4.48, 95% CI 3.41–5.89) and depression (aOR 3.09, 2.20–4.33); isolated sleepiness was most strongly associated with severe binge eating (BES ≥ 27: aOR 2.55, 1.69–3.83) and lower intuitive eating (IES-2 β = − 0.24, − 0.33 to − 0.15). The combined phenotype carried the highest risk overall. BMI did not differ across phenotypes. Findings were robust to OSA exclusion and to alternative insomnia thresholds. Conclusions. Insomnia and daytime sleepiness identify distinct behavioural phenotypes in clinical obesity, independently of BMI. Joint screening at intake may help personalise behavioural obesity management.

latest.title: Stigma and social stressors associated with female suicidal behaviors in Lahore Pakistan
latest.abstract: Abstract Objective This study aimed to determine the prevalence of suicidal ideation and attempts among women of reproductive age and examined their association with mental illness, as well as socioeconomic and cultural factors. The research also seeks to contribute to the de-stigmatization of women’s suicide, promote effective coping mechanisms, and strengthen the role of service providers in the prevention of suicide and attempted suicide in this population. Methodology: The study used a qualitative exploratory research design. This study was conducted at three tertiary-care hospitals of Lahore. By using purposive sampling, 15 female participants who had attempted suicide attempts, deliberated self-harm and suicidal ideations, and 5 services providers serving at the tertiary care hospital of Lahore were selected and interviewed. A semi-structured interview guide was developed and used to conduct the in-depth individual interviews.. Results The findings showed a strong correlation between social determinants such as poverty and increasing rates of suicide among women of reproductive age. The direct relationship between suicide and mental illness was not found, however, social stressors were contributing to the development of mental illness, particularly depression and anxiety, among women. Social support was associated with a lower risk of suicide attempts among women. No positive role of the health system was identified in this study. According to service providers, factors like convergence of socioeconomic hardships, gender disparity and health system gaps are the causes of suicide among Pakistani women. Conclusion The study found that while social support was protective, poor family dynamics and social stressors were major contributors to suicidal behavior among wom

latest.title: Success factors of university business incubators in Zimbabwe: staff perspectives on ecosystem orchestration in a resource-constrained environment
latest.abstract: Abstract In the African context, university-affiliated business incubators are increasingly taking positions as key mechanisms for venture creation and facilitating technology commercialisation. Nonetheless, the existing evidence regarding what makes them effective continues to be largely shaped by research conducted in developed countries. This study draws on an entrepreneurial ecosystem and stakeholder perspective and adopts an interpretivist, qualitative exploratory design to explore what incubator personnel perceive as the critical success factors of university business incubators in Zimbabwe, and how they perceive these factors to relate to one another. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with five key informants drawn purposively from the country’s three operational university incubators at the time of the study. The collected data were analysed thematically. Five interconnecting themes emerged. These include (1) funding as the foundational success factor, (2) stakeholder ecosystems and partnerships, (3) technical and mentorship support based on university expertise, (4) monitoring and evaluation systems as a source of legitimacy, and (5) contextual constraints arising from macroeconomic instability and institutional fragmentation. The findings suggest that where resources are constrained, the university staff associated university incubator effectiveness less with sophisticated venture financing mechanisms than with stakeholder orchestration, institutional legitimacy and hybrid support ecosystems. Such factors connect and synergise university, government, donor and private-sector resources. Implications for universities, incubator managers and policymakers are outlined.

latest.title: Navigating divorce and partner bereavement: Personality and trajectories of change in life satisfaction and mental health.
latest.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
latest.abstract: Dissolutions of romantic relationships can elicit diverse reactions across various aspects of well-being, but they also offer an opportunity to examine which factors promote resilience and identify individuals at risk. In this preregistered multi-sample longitudinal study, we examined the heterogeneity in life satisfaction and mental health changes around and during divorce or partner bereavement, and whether personality (i.e., traits and resilient versus nonresilient personality profiles) may explain individual differences in change trajectories. Data from 1,306 divorcees and 1,150 bereaved partners were drawn from nationally representative panel studies in the Netherlands (N = 12,551), Germany (N = 10,830), and China (N = 28,628), and analyzed using growth mixture modeling. Four life satisfaction trajectories and three mental health trajectories were identified for each event. Recovery and resilience emerged as the most common trajectories across events, outcomes, and samples. Among personality factors, neuroticism was the most consistent predictor of a lower likelihood of belonging to a resilience trajectory. This study advanced the generalizability of findings across diverse loss-based events, populations, and aspects of well-being. The findings further underscore the influence of neuroticism in shaping, and potentially complicating, psychological adjustment surrounding divorce and partner bereavement.

latest.title: Rompiendo ciclos intergeneracionales: Regulación emocional, apego seguro y bienestar infantil desde el enfoque de la Nueva Escuela Mexicana
latest.abstract: El bienestar emocional en la infancia constituye un factor determinante para el desarrollo integral de las personas, ya que influye en la forma en que los niños aprenden, se relacionan con los demás y enfrentan los desafíos de la vida cotidiana. La salud emocional de los adultos cuidadores incide directamente en la manera en que los niños aprenden a reconocer, expresar y regular sus propias emociones, dado que los menores aprenden principalmente a través de la observación e imitación de las conductas adultas. Cuando los adultos no han desarrollado habilidades de regulación afectiva o arrastran heridas emocionales no resueltas de su propia infancia, tienden a reproducir patrones disfuncionales en la crianza, lo que puede afectar la seguridad emocional y el bienestar de los niños a su cargo. El presente artículo de reflexión analiza la relación entre la salud emocional del adulto y el desarrollo del bienestar en la infancia, a partir de una revisión de la literatura especializada en psicología del desarrollo, teoría del apego y educación emocional. Se examina cómo las heridas emocionales no resueltas tienden a repetirse en la dinámica familiar, generando ciclos intergeneracionales que pueden prevenirse mediante procesos terapéuticos y educación emocional. La evidencia revisada sugiere que el bienestar emocional del adulto constituye una condición necesaria para ofrecer a la infancia entornos seguros y afectivamente nutritivos, lo que favorece la construcción de vínculos seguros y una autoestima saludable.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan dan Electronic Word of Mouth (eWOM) Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian pada Koka Ramen Express Sudirman
latest.venue: Jurnal Penelitian Ekonomi Manajemen dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: The increasingly competitive culinary industry requires businesses to improve service quality and manage their digital reputation to influence consumer purchasing decisions. This study aims to examine the effects of service quality and Electronic Word of Mouth (eWOM) on purchasing decisions among consumers of Koka Ramen Express Sudirman, both partially and simultaneously. This research employs a quantitative approach with a causal associative design. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using purposive sampling involving 120 respondents who had previously purchased and consumed products at Koka Ramen Express Sudirman. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics 29. The results indicate that service quality has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.207 and a significance level of less than 0.001. Electronic Word of Mouth also has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.184 and a significance level of less than 0.001. Simultaneously, both variables have a significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a coefficient of determination of 63.6%. Service quality is the more dominant factor influencing purchasing decisions compared to eWOM. These findings imply that management should improve employee friendliness, service speed, and restaurant cleanliness while optimizing social media activities and responding professionally to customer reviews to strengthen consumer confidence in making purchasing decisions.

latest.title: Analisis Daya Saing dan Kinerja Ekspor Karet Alam Indonesia dan Thailand di Pasar Korea Selatan
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis dan membandingkan keunggulan komparatif serta posisi spesialisasi perdagangan karet alam (HS 4001) antara Indonesia dan Thailand di pasar Korea Selatan periode 2016–2025. Menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif komparatif, data sekunder time-series bersumber dari ITC Trade Map dianalisis dengan metode Revealed Comparative Advantage (RCA), Revealed Symmetric Comparative Advantage (RSCA), dan Trade Specialization Index (TSI). Hasil analisis RSCA menunjukkan bahwa Indonesia (0,84–0,94) dan Thailand (0,93–0,97) secara konsisten memiliki keunggulan komparatif yang sangat kuat (RSCA > 0) di pasar Korea Selatan. Meskipun demikian, daya saing Thailand relatif lebih stabil dibanding Indonesia yang mengalami tren penurunan di paruh akhir pengamatan. Hasil analisis TSI mengonfirmasi bahwa kedua negara bertindak sebagai eksportir bersih (net exporter) utama dengan nilai mendekati 1,00. Fluktuasi moderat pada nilai TSI Indonesia merefleksikan adanya penyesuaian impor bahan baku guna memenuhi kebutuhan industri pengolahan hilir domestik. Untuk menjaga kesinambungan ekspor, kebijakan strategis perlu difokuskan pada peremajaan tanaman karet, efisiensi rantai pasok, standardisasi mutu, dan percepatan hilirisasi produk.

latest.title: Institutional complexity and post-acquisition integration in cross-border mergers and acquisitions: top management team deployment
Retrieval-Augmented Generation Chatbot for Academic Information Services Using GROQ API
latest.venue: TEKNOSAINS Jurnal Sains Teknologi dan Informatika
latest.abstract: Academic information services in universities are still largely carried out manually by administrative staff with limited working hours, making it difficult for students to receive quick responses, especially outside office hours. This study aims to design and implement an academic chatbot using the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach through the Groq API and a Streamlit interface. The system was developed following the Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, which includes problem identification, defining solution objectives, dataset collection, artifact design and development, system demonstration, testing and evaluation, as well as communication of research results. Black-box testing on 20 questions yielded 18 valid answers, while semantic quality evaluation using BERTScore produced a precision of 0.7054, recall of 0.7176, and F1-score of 0.7095. The average system response time was 1.45 seconds, with a median of 0.85 seconds, indicates that the majority of responses were provided in less than one second, despite a single outlier of 12.13 seconds. These results finding suggest that the integration of RAG with the Groq API holds potential for enhancing digital academic information services in higher education. Nevertheless, its operational benefits in real-world scenarios warrant further evaluation through empirical user testing.

latest.title: Bridging the gap between critical and applied approaches in the science of well-being: An analysis of evaluative subjective well-being measures
latest.abstract: This article examines three recurring arguments for evaluative subjective well-being (swb) measures: instruments that ask respondents to broadly assess their lives, such as the Cantril Ladder and general life satisfaction questions. To organise the debate and support better dialogue between critics and supporters of these instruments, we draw on two conceptual tools from the philosophy of well-being: the distinction between constitutive and determinative questions, and the characterisation of well-being as a thick concept. The first argument we analyse holds that leaving the object undefined is desirable (a "non-paternalistic" approach). We argue that this stance legitimately declines the constitutive question about well-being, but that in delegating it to respondents it makes engagement with that question a precondition for interpreting the resulting scores. The second argument holds that the absence of a clear definition is not disqualifying, given large samples, respondents' familiarity with the relevant expressions, and the instruments' psychometric properties. We argue that each support admits an alternative explanation grounded in the social rules governing well-being talk, and that no thin, purely descriptive construct lies beneath the everyday expressions these measures rely on. The third argument holds that the measures are useful regardless of these limitations. Here we distinguish an agnostic stance, for which scores are a means of predicting other outcomes, from a score-as-target stance, for which raising the scores is itself the end. The agnostic stance declines constitutive questions successfully, at the price of abandoning well-being as the central object of research; the score-as-target stance cannot, since it must still say why this quantity rather than

latest.title: Knowledge Management Capabilities and Performance of Tier 1 Deposit-Taking SACCOs in Kenya
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
latest.abstract: The main objective of this study was to determine the influence of knowledge management capabilities on the performance of Tier 1 Deposit-Taking SACCOs (DT-SACCOs) in Kenya. Knowledge management capabilities were conceptualized as a second-order dynamic capability comprising knowledge acquisition, knowledge sharing and knowledge application. A mixed methods approach was applied, drawing data from finance, audit, credit, Front Office Service Activity (FOSA), marketing, and Information and Communication Technology (ICT) management staff across the 42 Tier 1 DT-SACCOs licensed by the Sacco Societies Regulatory Authority (SASRA) in Kenya. A census approach was adopted, and data were collected using structured questionnaires and analyzed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), with descriptive statistics and simple linear regression guiding interpretation. The descriptive findings indicated moderate adoption of knowledge management practices, with item means ranging from 2.09 to 3.46. Knowledge management capabilities were found to enhance collaboration, information sharing and decision-making, although limited knowledge application and weak knowledge-tracking mechanisms restricted optimal performance gains. Simple linear regression established that knowledge management capabilities had a statistically significant and positive influence on performance, explaining 56.8% of the variance in performance (R² = .568, Adjusted R² = .566, F(1, 249) = 327.248, p < .001; B = .719, β = .754, t = 18.090, p < .001), leading to rejection of the null hypothesis. The study recommends strategic prioritisation of knowledge management systems, particularly knowledge application and knowledge-tracking mechanisms, to improve competitiveness, operational resilience and susta

latest.title: From barriers to breakthroughs: Navigating success drivers of women entrepreneurs in China
latest.abstract: Despite the adolescence stage, the past 30 years have evidenced the proliferation of mainstream academic research for the most interesting and emerging phenomenon, ‘Women Entrepreneurship’. To further shed light on the above-stated phenomenon, this study aims to explore the success drivers and challenges of women entrepreneurs in the specific context of China. For this, success drivers and challenges are treated as antecedents (independent variables), entrepreneurial innovative behavior and government support as moderating variables, and the success of women entrepreneurs is taken as the outcome (dependent variable). To address the aforementioned research agenda, data were gathered from the women entrepreneurs of SMEs located in China who are successfully running their business for at least 3 years. A total of 260 survey responses (free from missing values) were obtained from specific the sample of women entrepreneurs (showing 67% response rate). SPSS 23.00 was used to test the hypothesis about the direct and indirect association of success drivers, challenges, entrepreneurial innovative behavior, Government support and the success of women entrepreneurs. Results revealed that the specific constructs of success drivers and challenges significantly affect the success of women entrepreneurs. Furthermore, entrepreneurial innovative behavior and Government support have also been proven as statistically significant moderators to strengthen the direct association of specific aforementioned constructs. This study is purely unique in theoretical and practical aspects as it addressed the empirically petite-researched phenomenon ‘women entrepreneurship’ specifically in the context of China. The study expanded the normal inquiry mode by looking into the moderated framework of entr

latest.title: Digital and social media marketing: a bibliometric mapping from 2020 to 2025
latest.abstract: Abstract Digital and social media marketing is reshaping how firms communicate with consumers, gather market intelligence, manage customer journeys, and build brand relationships. This study followed the PRISMA framework to select relevant Scopus-indexed articles between 2020 and 2025 under the business, management, and accounting subject area, using the search terms “digital marketing” and “social media marketing” in titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search, conducted on 20 February 2026 and restricted to open-access, English-language, final-stage journal articles, yielded 1,054 articles. Performance analysis, citation analysis, author-keyword co-occurrence mapping, an average-publication-year overlay, co-citation analysis, and bibliographic coupling were conducted using VOSviewer. Findings reveal publication growth, particularly during 2024 and 2025. Indonesia was the leading country by publications, whereas the UK was the most influential country by citations. Additionally, the “Journal of Business Research” is the most influential, while “Cogent Business & Management” is the most productive journal; the most-cited document is “Setting the future of digital and social media marketing research: Perspectives and research propositions,” with 1,806 citations, produced by “International Journal of Information Management.” Four of the ten prominent authors published six papers each, including Saura, J.R., and Huertas-Garcia, R., both affiliated with Spanish institutions. Keyword mapping identifies digital marketing, social media marketing, social media, consumer behavior, marketing, and purchase intention as central themes. This study clarifies the post-2020 knowledge structure of the open-access segment of this literature, proposes that digital and social media marketi

latest.title: Shared molecular and immune signatures of tic disorders and allergic diseases: a cross-disease transcriptomic analysis
latest.abstract: Background Tic disorders (TD) are epidemiologically associated with allergic diseases, but the peripheral molecular features potentially shared by these conditions remain unclear. This study aimed to identify overlapping peripheral blood transcriptomic features across independent TD and allergic disease cohorts and to explore their associations with peripheral immune signatures. Methods Two independent Gene Expression Omnibus whole-blood transcriptomic datasets, GSE310998 (28 individuals with TD and 20 controls) and GSE141661 (248 individuals with allergic diseases and 209 controls), were analyzed using differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis for exploratory cross-disease candidate-gene prioritization. Reactome GSEA, ssGSEA, and CIBERSORT were used to characterize associated pathway and immune features. Male BALB/c mice were assigned to control, OVA-sensitized, IDPN-treated, or combined-treatment groups (n = 8 per group). Stereotypy, OVA-specific IgE, whole-blood Gpx7 mRNA, and the percentage of CD63-positive neutrophils were assessed. Results Exploratory integrative analysis prioritized GPX7 as a candidate gene for further investigation. The GPX7-low groups showed more pronounced neutrophil-related immune features in both datasets. The combined-treatment group exhibited higher stereotypy scores than the IDPN group, alongside lower whole-blood Gpx7 mRNA and a higher percentage of CD63-positive neutrophils than either single-treatment group. Conclusion These findings identify overlapping peripheral transcriptomic and neutrophil-related immune features across independent TD and allergic disease cohorts. Although the functional relationship between GPX7 expression and neutrophil-related alterations remains to be established, these

latest.title: Analisys detection place defect incoming part in the incoming quality control division at PT XYZ cikarang
latest.venue: TEKNOSAINS Jurnal Sains Teknologi dan Informatika
latest.abstract: The quality of incoming parts is a critical factor affecting the quality of final products in the electronics manufacturing industry. Nonconforming materials received from suppliers can increase product defects, production costs, and disrupt manufacturing processes. This study aims to analyze incoming part defects in the Incoming Quality Control (IQC) Division of PT XYZ Cikarang based on defect types, defect detection locations, root causes, and improvement priorities. The study employed Seven Tools, Fishbone Diagram, and Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA) using data from the Incoming Production Rework Report for February 2026. The data were analyzed using check sheets, Pareto diagrams, defect detection place analysis, Fishbone diagrams, and FMEA. The results revealed that scratch was the dominant defect, accounting for 58.66% of the 358 recorded defects, while the highest-risk failure cause was the non-optimal material handling standard operating procedure, with a Risk Priority Number (RPN) of 504. Based on these findings, improvement priorities were focused on revising material handling procedures, enhancing operator competency, standardizing supplier packing methods, and improving material storage systems. This study contributes by integrating Seven Tools, Fishbone Diagram, and FMEA to establish a systematic risk-based approach for prioritizing quality improvement actions, thereby supporting more effective incoming material quality control in electronics manufacturing

latest.title: Hybrid Markov Regime-Switching and Hurdle modeling of last-mile livestock logistics in Ukraine under systemic volatility
latest.abstract: Abstract This study examines the transformation of last-mile logistics in Ukraine’s livestock supply chains under conditions of prolonged systemic volatility and infrastructure disruption. A hybrid analytical framework is proposed that integrates Random Forest Recursive Feature Elimination (RF-RFE) for preliminary predictor screening, a two-state Markov Regime-Switching (MRS) model for identifying latent logistics regimes, and a two-part Hurdle model for separately estimating disruption probability and conditional freight-cost intensity. The empirical analysis uses a verified monthly panel dataset covering 2023–2025 across three contrasting regional logistics nodes - Kyiv, Vinnytsia, and Lviv - and incorporates energy, security, market, transport, and infrastructure-related indicators. The MRS results identify two statistically distinct and persistent freight-cost regimes, with the systemic-crisis regime characterized by a 21.8% higher mean Freight Cost Per Ton and a longer expected duration than the operational-stability regime. The Hurdle estimates show that Security Alerts and Power Outage Hours are positively associated with the probability of logistics disruption, while Power Outage Hours and Fuel Price Volatility are positively associated with conditional freight-cost intensity; regional comparisons further reveal heterogeneous exposure to systemic shocks. Counterfactual technological scenarios further indicate that combining AI-assisted dynamic routing with decentralized autonomous and light electric transport solutions could reduce the estimated sensitivity of freight costs to energy disruptions by approximately 24.2%. The findings demonstrate the value of combining latent-regime identification, sequential disruption modeling, and technological scenario analysis

latest.title: Linking personality to COVID-19 attitudes, concerns and biosafety behaviors: meta-analytic foundations for future pandemic preparedness
latest.abstract: Knowledge of behavioral reactions to the COVID-19 pandemic can help manage future reactions and biosafety behaviors, potentially altering the course of future epidemics and pandemics. Personality traits play a role in creating safe environments. We examined the Big Five and Dark Triad personality trait families' associations with biosafety behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic, a period characterized by strong situational pressures. We also examined personality's associations with COVID-19 concerns and attitudes. Associations with biosafety behaviors, including hygiene, social distancing, self-quarantining, avoiding exposures, and preparatory behaviors, were examined in 92 independent samples comprising 973 effect sizes from over 50 countries. Different traits served different functions: conscientiousness and agreeableness predicted prosocial protective behaviors such as social distancing and hygiene, neuroticism was strongly associated with pandemic-related concerns but not behaviors, and extraversion and openness were linked to adaptation to new safety protocols. Dark Triad traits showed negative associations with collective biosafety behaviors but positive associations with preparatory behaviors, a finding consistent with pandemic responses motivated by self-interest rather than collective welfare. Despite strong situational constraints, personality maintained meaningful associations with behavior. Meta-analytic evidence indicates COVID-19 attitudes, concerns, and biosafety behaviors are in part predicted by personality traits, with implications for public health messaging and understanding individual differences in biosafety-critical occupations.

latest.title: Social Determinants of Health Associated With Unhealthy Weight Management Behaviors Among Emerging Adult Women: Nationwide Cross-Sectional Study
latest.abstract: Abstract Background Unhealthy weight management behaviors (UWMBs) have become increasingly common among emerging adult women, yet prior research has largely focused on psychological or perceptual correlates in isolation. In appearance-oriented contexts, structural influences, including social norms, may co-occur with individual characteristics to shape these behaviors. The social determinants of health (SDOH) framework offers a useful lens for examining UWMBs by jointly considering structural and intermediary determinants. Objective This study aimed to identify key SDOH associated with engagement in UWMBs among emerging adult women in South Korea by examining structural and intermediary determinants within a single adjusted model. Methods A nationwide cross-sectional survey was conducted among women aged 19 to 25 years using stratified sampling with quota allocation based on residential area and employment status. The final analytic sample included 1594 participants. UWMBs were assessed using a 9-item checklist; reporting at least 1 behavior in the past year was classified as UWMB engagement. Structural determinants included social norms, social influence, and socioeconomic position. Intermediary determinants included perceived body shape, body weight misperception, weight disparity, weight self-stigma, media health literacy, social network support, and BMI. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with UWMBs. Results Overall, 88% (1404/1594) of participants reported at least 1 UWMB in the past year, and 71.4% (n=1002) engaged in 2 or more UWMBs. latest.title: ФОРМУВАННЯ КОГНІТИВНИХ ЯКОСТЕЙ ЛІДЕРА У ВІЙСЬКОВОМУ КОЛЕКТИВІ
latest.abstract: Стаття присвячена аналізу психологічних механізмів формування когнітивних якостей лідера у військовому колективі з урахуванням специфіки професійної діяльності військовослужбовців, а також обґрунтуванню ефективних методів і засобів розвитку цих якостей у майбутніх та діючих командирів. Розглянуто індивідуально-психологічні та соціально-групові чинники, що впливають на становлення таких когнітивних характеристик, як аналітичне та критичне мислення, когнітивна гнучкість, здатність до прийняття рішень в умовах невизначеності, метапізнання, саморегуляція та когнітивна стійкість. Досліджено міжфункціональну взаємодію інтелектуальної, емоційно-вольової та психофізіологічної сфер особистості військовослужбовця, де сила нервової системи, обсяг оперативної пам’яті та резилієнтність виступають фундаментальними ознаками управлінського потенціалу. Особливу увагу приділено впливу бойового стресу на когнітивні процеси командира та психологічним умовам збереження ефективності мислення в екстремальних ситуаціях. Розкрито ризики звуження обсягу уваги, виникнення «тунельного бачення» та деструктивного впливу дефіциту сну і сенсорного навантаження на якість тактичних оцінок. У статті наголошується, що лідер у військовому колективі – це не лише особа, яка займає офіційну посаду командира, а й той, хто має внутрішній авторитет, здатний впливати на настрої, поведінку та ефективність дій підлеглих. Когнітивна сфера відіграє ключову роль у цьому процесі, забезпечуючи об’єктивне сприйняття реальності, оцінювання ризиків і командну координацію. В умовах воєнної діяльності, де рішення часто приймаються за дефіциту часу, інформації та під сильним психофізіологічним навантаженням, здатність до швидкої обробки даних, системного аналізу та прогнозування наслідків набуває критичного значення. latest.title: The motivational gain control effect: mechanisms of predictive load and brand signal-to-noise ratio on danmaku interaction with AI advertising
latest.abstract: Purpose This study develops the motivational gain control model, examining how dual cognitive demands of AI-generated advertising – internal decoding burden from structural transitions and external attributional ambiguity from executional convergence – jointly influence real-time audience interaction. Predictive load captures expectation-updating demand across adjacent stages; brand signal-to-noise ratio (BSNR) captures attributional clarity relative to competitors, constituting two dimensions of cognitive decoding valence whose evaluative meaning depends on product involvement. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from 248 AI-generated advertisements and their danmaku interactions – synchronous viewer comments overlaid on video – on a major Chinese video platform, each divided into five periods, a panel vector error correction model estimates short-run and long-run effects and product involvement's moderating role. Findings For low-involvement products, content-level predictive load suppresses danmaku interaction while BSNR enhances it across both horizons. For high-involvement products, the positive effect of BSNR is significantly attenuated, whereas the negative effect of predictive load is only marginally attenuated, mainly in the long run. The BSNR attenuation provides strong evidence against a pure resource-depletion account; the predictive load attenuation, though marginally significant, is directionally consistent. Together, these patterns support motivation-dependent valence reassessment. Cross-modal congruence exhibits non-monotonic temporal patterns distinct from content-level features. Originality/value This study provides evidence against the fixed valence assumption shared across processing fluency, competitive interference and elaboration likeliho

latest.title: The Impact of Profitability, Credit Risk, Liquidity Risk, and Efficiency Risk on Sharia Commercial Bank Stability (2021–2025)
latest.venue: Jurnal Ekonomi Islam Akuntansi dan Manajemen
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of profitability, credit risk, liquidity risk, and efficiency risk on the stability of Sharia Commercial Banks in Indonesia during the 2021-2025 period. Bank stability in this study is proxied by the Z-score, while profitability is measured by Return on Assets, credit risk by Non-Performing Financing, liquidity risk by the Financing-to-Deposit Ratio, and efficiency risk by the Operating Expenses to Operating Income ratio. A quantitative approach is employed using secondary data derived from the financial statements of Sharia Commercial Banks for the 2021-2025 period. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 10 Sharia Commercial Banks that met the study's criteria. Data analysis was conducted using panel data regression with the aid of EViews. The results indicate that profitability does not have a significant effect on the stability of Sharia Commercial Banks. Credit risk and liquidity risk both have a significant effect on bank stability, whereas efficiency risk (proxied by the operating expenses to operating income ratio) does not. Collectively, profitability, credit risk, liquidity risk, and efficiency risk significantly influence the stability of Sharia Commercial Banks. The coefficient of determination of 91.9984% indicates that the variation in bank stability can be explained by the variables in the research model, while the remainder is explained by factors outside the model.

latest.title: Cost Management Accounting Practices and Financing Decisions Debt Vs Equity Among Nigerian SMES
latest.venue: JOURNAL OF ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
latest.abstract: Small and Medium Enterprises constitute the backbone of the Nigerian economy, accounting for approximately 96% of businesses, 84% of employment, and 48% of Gross Domestic Product [GDP] (National Bureau of Statistics [NBS] & Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria [SMEDAN], 2021). Despite this significant contribution, over 80% of Nigerian SMEs fail within the first five years of operation (Akingbade, 2014). A major factor responsible for this high failure rate is poor financial management, particularly in the areas of cost control and access to finance. While cost management accounting practices provide the internal data needed for efficiency and profitability, financing decisions determine how SMEs fund growth and expansion. However, there is limited empirical evidence on how these two critical areas interact, especially within the Nigerian context where SMEs face high interest rates, stringent collateral requirements, and an underdeveloped equity market. [SMEs] This study therefore examined the influence of cost management accounting practices on financing decisions: debt versus equity among Nigerian SMEs across the six geopolitical zones. The broad objective was to determine the extent to which cost management practices influence SME financing choices. The specific objectives were to: examine the extent of adoption of cost management accounting practices among Nigerian SMEs; assess the factors influencing debt financing decisions; assess the factors influencing equity financing decisions; determine the influence of cost management accounting practices on the choice between debt and equity financing; and examine the future outlook of SME owners and managers regarding cost management and access to financing. The study was anchored on three theories.

latest.title: The Effect of Brand Equity on Patient Loyalty with Patient Satisfaction as a Mediating Variable in Inpatient Services
latest.abstract: Low inpatient utilization, reflected in a suboptimal Bed Occupancy Rate (BOR), remains a critical challenge for hospital management. Strengthening brand equity is increasingly recognized as a strategic approach to enhance patient loyalty and improve service utilization. This study aimed to examine the effect of brand equity on patient loyalty, with patient satisfaction as a mediating variable, among inpatients at RSI Siti Aisyah Madiun. A quantitative cross-sectional design was conducted involving 100 inpatients selected through purposive sampling during the discharge process. Data were collected using a structured 5-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression and the Sobel test for mediation analysis. The results demonstrated that brand equity had a significant positive effect on both patient satisfaction (p < 0.05) and patient loyalty (p < 0.05). Patient satisfaction also significantly influenced patient loyalty (p < 0.05). Furthermore, mediation analysis confirmed that patient satisfaction partially mediated the relationship between brand equity and patient loyalty. In conclusion, brand equity plays a pivotal role in strengthening patient retention, both directly and indirectly through patient satisfaction. Hospital management should prioritize brand-building strategies integrated with consistent service quality to optimize patient satisfaction, foster long-term loyalty, and ultimately elevate inpatient service utilization and BOR.

latest.title: Analysis Of The Influence Of Employee Engagement And Self-Efficacy On Turnover Intention (A Case Study Of Employees at Golden Street Food Tasikmalaya
latest.venue: Jurnal Ekonomi Islam Akuntansi dan Manajemen
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the relationship between Employee Engagement and Self-Efficacy and Turnover Intention among employees of Golden Street Food Tasikmalaya. This research employed a quantitative method with a causal approach. A saturated sampling technique was used, involving 41 employees as respondents. Data were collected through observation, interviews, documentation, and questionnaires. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of SPSS version 25. Hypothesis testing was conducted using the F-test and t-test at a significance level of α = 0.05 (5%). The results indicate that Employee Engagement and Self-Efficacy simultaneously have no significant effect on Turnover Intention. Furthermore, the partial test results show that Employee Engagement has no significant effect on Turnover Intention. Likewise, Self-Efficacy also has no significant effect on Turnover Intention.

latest.title: The theoretical and applied implications of self-compassion in the Career Construction Model of Adaptation
latest.abstract: Emotional processes underlying career adaptability remain underexplored. The Career Construction Model of Adaptation (CCMA) asserts that psychological resources of concern, curiosity, control, and confidence promote successful career transitions. This conceptual paper proposes a potential fifth adaptive resource, self-compassion, within the Career Construction Model of Adaptation. Self-compassion adds novelty to the model by theorizing an emotional mechanism that may promote successful career transitions. The proposed theoretical framework differentiates self-compassion from the original adaptive resources and uses a fictional vignette to illustrate clinical application. Limitations of the proposed model are acknowledged. Research, clinical, educational, and organizational implications are discussed.

latest.title: Explaining Human Psychology Evolutionarily: Recent Criticisms and New Lines of Defense
latest.abstract: Abstract Evolutionary psychology aims to fulfil Darwin’s vision—articulated towards the end of The Origin of Species— of providing a new foundation for the scientific study of human psychology. The field holds that human behavior should be explained using the same biological principles and empirical approaches applied to non-human animals, emphasizing how different evolutionary forces have influenced the functioning of their psychological mechanisms. Scholarly debate has long centered on issues such as adaptationism, testability, cognitive modularity, and the role of culture. More recently, however, evolutionary psychology has faced a new wave of critiques. These include that it presupposes, but cannot support, that human psychological mechanisms are “vertically homologous” with those of their ancestors; that it neglects several important evolutionary processes; that it relies on an outdated computationalist view of the mind; and that it does not yet satisfy the criteria for a mature, normal science. This article aims to present a balanced account of these emerging critiques, along with a set of original responses that, to date, have not been fully articulated in the literature. In general, we argue that the critiques involve unsound argumentation with false premises, attack a straw man position, are vulnerable to reductios , or rely on an implausible philosophical model of how scientific works ought to be evaluated.

latest.title: Frequency and Factors Associated with Preoperative Anxiety Specific to Anesthesia in Patients awaiting Surgery in Kinshasa
latest.venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
latest.abstract: Background: Preoperative anxiety related to anesthesia can affect patients' psychological preparation and perioperative care. Data regarding anesthesia-specific anxiety in Kinshasa remain limited. This study assessed its frequency and associated factors in adult surgical patients. Methods: A prospective, analytical, multicenter study was conducted in four hospitals in Kinshasa between May 2025 and August 2026. A total of 443 adult patients were consecutively recruited. Anxiety and information needs related to anesthesia were assessed using the Amsterdam Preoperative Anxiety and Information Scale (APAIS). Associated factors were analyzed using binary logistic regression. Results: Preoperative anxiety specific to anesthesia was identified in 212 patients (48%). A university education level was associated with an increased likelihood of anxiety (aOR = 18.5; 95% CI: 8.5 to 40.2), while prior experience with anesthesia (aOR = 0.4; 95% CI: 0.3 to 0.8) and detailed explanations received during the pre-anesthetic consultation (aOR = 0.04; 95% CI: 0.02 to 0.09) were associated with a lower likelihood. Moderate information needs were associated with an increased likelihood of anxiety (aOR = 2.14; 95% CI: 1.1 to 4.2). Conclusion: Preoperative anxiety specific to anesthesia affected nearly half of the patients studied. Educational level, anesthetic history, pre-anesthetic detailed explanations, and information needs were independently associated with anxiety. Personalized preoperative communication and a systematic assessment of information needs could improve patient preparation for anesthesia.

latest.title: Network analysis of physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress among Chinese university students
latest.abstract: Objective Physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress may be interconnected among university students, but their dimension-specific associations remain unclear. This study examined their network structure and compared male and female networks. Methods A convenience sample of 1,600 university students from two higher-education institutions in central China was surveyed from 16 March to 29 May 2026. Physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress were assessed using the Physical Activity Rating Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and 21-item Depression Anxiety Stress Scales. A 12-node regularized partial correlation network was estimated. Expected influence, bridge expected influence, bootstrap procedures, and network comparison tests were used. Results The network retained 27 non-zero edges, with stronger connections mainly within domains. Daytime dysfunction–stress had the largest positive cross-domain edge-weight point estimate, whereas exercise frequency–stress and exercise duration–subjective sleep quality were prominent negative connections. Stress showed relatively high expected influence and positive bridge expected influence point estimates, although bootstrap difference tests did not clearly distinguish these estimates from those of several other nodes. No gender-related differences were detected in global strength, network structure, or individual edges after multiple-comparison correction, while supplementary analyses indicated limited detection capability. Conclusions Cross-domain associations among physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress were concentrated in a limited number of dimensions, particularly stress, daytime dysfunction, exercise frequency, and exercise duration. latest.title: Descriptive Supply Chain Analytics and Performance of Large Manufacturing Firms in Kenya
latest.venue: International Journal of Supply Chain and Logistics
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study examined the influence of descriptive analytics on the performance of large manufacturing firms in Kenya, focusing on inventory situation reporting, demand context visualization, and purchase pattern analysis. Methodology: Anchored on resource dependence theory, the study adopted a mixed-methods research design. Mixed-methods research design integrates both qualitative and quantitative research approaches in the processes of data collection, analysis, and presentation. The target population for this study was 461 large manufacturing firms. Data was collected from a sample of 210 respondents out of a sample of 222, representing a (94.5%) response rate. Reliability and validity were confirmed through Cronbach's alpha (α > 0.70), KMO, and Bartlett's tests. Findings: Descriptive analytics constructs were widely practiced, with inventory situation reporting and purchase pattern analysis being the most embraced. Approximately 59% of respondents rated descriptive analytics as effective in improving performance of large manufacturing firms. Regression analysis confirmed a positive and significant relationship (R = 0.660, R² = 0.436, Beta = 0.734, p < 0.001), indicating that 43.6% of performance variation can be explained by descriptive analytics. Unique Contribution to Theory, Policy and Practice: This study serves as a foundational reference point for practitioners and policymakers alike. By delineating the pathways through which analytics enhance transparency and competitiveness. Policy makers and regulatory agencies must mandate that firms establish rigorous guidelines for the selection and utilization of analytic tools. latest.title: The Effect Of Expertise And Infrastructure On The Performance Of Civil Servants In The Regional Revenue Agency Of Tasikmalaya City
latest.venue: Journal of Management Economic and Accounting
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of expertise and infrastructure on the performance of civil servants at the Tasikmalaya City Regional Revenue Agency. The research method used is a quantitative method with an associative approach. The population in the study amounted to 57 employees and all of them were sampled using the total sampling technique. Data analysis was carried out using multiple linear regression using the SPSS version 25 support application. The test results show that simultaneously indicate the variables used in the study, namely expertise and infrastructure on the performance of civil servants at the Tasikmalaya City Regional Revenue Agency. Likewise, partially there is a significant influence of expertise and infrastructure on employee performance.

latest.title: Can Coastal Ecological Restoration Promote Corporate ESG Performance? Evidence from China’s Blue Bay Remediation Action
latest.abstract: Coastal ecological degradation poses wide-ranging challenges to marine ecosystems and the sustainable development of coastal economies. However, evidence on whether public ecological restoration policies influence corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance remains limited. This study examines China’s Blue Bay Remediation Action (BBRA), launched in 2016, as a quasi-natural experiment to assess its effects on the ESG performance of Chinese listed maritime firms. Using panel data on China’s A-share listed maritime companies from 2008 to 2021 and a PSM-IPW-DID design, we find a statistically significant positive effect of the BBRA on overall ESG scores. Positive effects are also statistically significant for the environmental and governance scores. Additional analyses indicate that BBRA implementation is associated with increased environmental subsidies, reduced financing constraints, stronger environmental regulation, and greater institutional investor attention. The positive effects are more pronounced among non-state-owned firms, firms in southern coastal regions, and firms located in cities with higher public environmental concern. The findings provide empirical evidence on the relationship between ecological restoration policies and corporate sustainable development, along with policy insights for improving coastal ecological governance and supporting firms’ green transition in China.

latest.title: Digital maturity, green HR analytics, and sustainable logistics performance in agri-food supply chains
latest.abstract: Introduction Digital and environmental transformation increasingly converge in agri-food cold-chain logistics, yet how digital capabilities relate to frontline loss-prevention practices remains unclear. Drawing on the Twin Transition perspective, this study examined the associations among digital maturity, green human resource analytics (GHRA), employee green loss-prevention behavior, and supervisor-rated sustainable logistics performance. It also examined whether the association between GHRA and employee behavior varied with perceived algorithmic pressure. Methods This cross-sectional study analyzed matched questionnaire data from 96 supervisors and 545 employees across 96 Chinese agri-food cold-chain firms or departments. The primary analysis used a pooled single-level structural equation model. Sensitivity analyses used composite-score mixed models and unit-level cluster bootstrapping to assess the influence of clustering. Results Digital maturity was positively associated with GHRA, which in turn was positively associated with employee green loss-prevention behavior. This behavior was positively associated with supervisor-rated sustainable logistics performance. The direct association between GHRA and performance was statistically nonsignificant. Positive indirect estimates were consistent with the proposed pathways linking GHRA to performance through employee behavior and linking digital maturity to performance through GHRA and employee behavior in sequence. The positive association between GHRA and employee behavior was weaker at higher levels of perceived algorithmic pressure. The sensitivity analyses supported the overall pattern of associations. latest.title: Implementing game-based and quest technologies in secondary school geography: a quasi-experimental study of 7th-grade learning outcomes in Kazakhstan
latest.abstract: The modernization of school education in Central Asia has placed innovative learning technologies at the center of national education policy, yet evidence on how such technologies perform in ordinary classrooms remains scarce. This study examined whether the systematic use of game-based and quest technologies in Grade 7 geography lessons is associated with higher student achievement than conventional instruction. A quasi-experiment with a repeated cross-sectional design was conducted over three academic years (2017–2020) in two state secondary schools in the Zhambyl region of Kazakhstan: a new Grade 7 cohort was assessed in each school at a baseline stage and at two formative stages. The experimental group ( n = 45 per stage, School No. 28 named after A. Moldagulova, Taraz) studied geography through a program of didactic games, educational quests, and interactive tasks embedded in short-term lesson plans, while the control group ( n = 55 per stage, A. Makarenko Secondary School, Zhambyl district) followed the standard curriculum. Achievement was taken from criterion-based assessment and classified into low, medium, and high levels. At baseline the achievement distributions of the two groups were similar [χ 2 (2) = 0.42, p = 0.809]. Across stages, the share of high-achieving students in the experimental group rose from 20.0% to 35.5% (two-sided p = 0.099) and changed little in the control group (from 23.6% to 25.4%); the difference-in-differences was +13.7 percentage points (95% CI −10.6 to 38.0, p = 0.268). Neither the between-group contrast at the final stage [χ 2 (2) = 1.67, p = 0.434] nor the group × stage interaction in an ordinal regression (OR = 1.30, 95% CI 0.76–2.21, p = 0.333) was statistically significant.
