latest.title: AI-Powered E-Commerce Solutions for Smarter Retail Management and Customer Engagement
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Running an ecommerce business involves more than displaying products and processing orders. Retailers must understand customer preferences, maintain accurate product information, manage inventory, and provide timely assistance across multiple channels. As product catalogues and customer expectations grow, managing these activities manually becomes increasingly difficult. An AI E-Commerce Development Company can help businesses introduce intelligent tools that simplify retail operations, improve product discovery, and create more relevant customer experiences. Using AI to Understand Customer Behaviour Customer behaviour provides useful information about what shoppers need and how they interact with an online store. Product views, search queries, cart activity, and purchase history can reveal patterns that help businesses improve their services. AI-based analytics can process these signals to identify customer interests and purchasing trends. For example, an online retailer may use customer activity to understand which product categories receive the most attention or where shoppers frequently leave the purchasing journey. An AI-enabled ecommerce platform can support: Customer segmentation Purchase pattern analysis Personalised product suggestions Shopping behaviour insights Cart abandonment analysis Campaign performance evaluation These insights can help marketing and ecommerce teams make more informed decisions. However, recommendations should be based on relevant, appropriately collected data rather than assumptions about individual customers. latest.title: THE FUTURE OF BANKING: FINTECH REGULATION AND TRANSFORMATION OF FINANCIAL SERVICES IN NIGERIA
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The Study appraised the Future of Banking: Fintech, Regulation and Transformation of Financial System, analyzing the implication for traditional financial institutions. Methodologically, survey design was employed with data sourced from selected account holders of both Fintech and traditional banks in Ikot Ekpene Local Government area metropolis. Beside the use of questionnaire, personal observations were carried out as data collection technique in addition to the secondary data sourced from relevant textbooks, journals, newspaper and Internet. Moreover, the study assessed the rating of respondents on customer services provided by both Fintech and traditional banks. As well, the identifiable customer services gaps in traditional banks were assessed. Moreso, findings revealed that Fintech and traditional banks differ significantly on customer services with notable areas of customer satisfactory services provided by Fintech over traditional banks to include faster and more accessibility to credit, easy account opening and set-ups, convenience and stress free, instant transfers, friendliness, innovative solution to the needs of customers, digital inclusion penetration with youth population and cordial customer relationship (addressing complaint swiftly). On service gaps in traditional banks, the study identified inefficient modern banking techniques, unreliable digital infrastructure and relative financial inclusion. In light of the findings, the study recommended that the traditional banks should develop modern banking technique such as artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning in financial service, invest aggressively in technology. latest.title: Experiential branding in the digital age: evaluative and experiential pathways from brand experience to customer satisfaction
latest.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study examines the psychological mechanisms linking brand experience and customer satisfaction. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S-O-R) framework and appraisal theory, it investigates the mediating roles of brand authenticity and brand engagement, treated, respectively, as an evaluative (cognitive-appraisal) and a multidimensional experiential-investment organismic pathway. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 304 smartphone consumers in Haryana NCR (India) using a structured questionnaire and a non-probability convenience sample. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM, SmartPLS 4) was used to test the model, which incorporates two reflective higher-order constructs and two mediators modelled in parallel (a formative Mode B re-estimation of the higher-order constructs, a sensitivity analysis with and without one affection item and a bootstrap contrast of the two specific indirect effects were added as robustness checks and a formal comparison). One indicator (AFFBENG3; loading 0.376) was removed post hoc; the structural results are the same when it is retained. Findings Brand experience is positively related to customer satisfaction, brand authenticity and brand engagement. Brand engagement ( β = 0.424) and brand authenticity ( β = 0.128) are both positively related to satisfaction, with engagement showing the numerically larger coefficient. Both specific indirect effects are significant (through engagement β = 0.107; through authenticity β = 0.048) alongside a significant direct path (β = 0.136), a pattern consistent with complementary partial mediation through two mediators modelled in parallel; because the direct path is small, this classification is treated cautiously. latest.title: Delving into AI disclosure architecture: Building trust in Indonesian telemedicine advertising
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractAI disclosure has become increasingly important in digital advertising, particularly in high-risk services such as telemedicine, where consumers evaluate message quality alongside provider accountability. This study aimed to examine how AI disclosure architecture, reflected in disclosure timing, disclosure specificity, and human control, influences perceived authenticity, message credibility, brand trust, and usage intention in Indonesian telemedicine advertising. A quantitative scenario-based online experiment used a 2 × 2 × 2 between-subjects design with 527 valid respondents. Data were analyzed using three-way factorial ANOVA, confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modelling, and bootstrap analysis with 5,000 resamples. Early disclosure, high specificity, and stated professional review or oversight produced more favourable evaluations across the disclosure conditions examined. Human control generated the largest main effects on perceived authenticity (partial η² = 0.346), message credibility (partial η² = 0.316), brand trust (partial η² = 0.318), and usage intention (partial η² = 0.166). Perceived authenticity increased brand trust (β = 0.304, p < 0.001), message credibility had a stronger effect on brand trust (β = 0.598, p < 0.001), and brand trust increased usage intention (β = 0.736, p < 0.001). Timing and specificity showed significant indirect effects on brand trust, while human control showed both direct and indirect effects. The effects were predominantly additive, with only a small timing × human-control interaction for message credibility (partial η² = 0.009). These findings indicate that, when AI disclosure is present, timing, specificity, and stated professional oversight provide distinct trust-relev

latest.title: MEASURING TOURISM PRICES USING TOURISM SATELLITE ACCOUNT WEIGHTS: A TOURISM PRICE INDEX FOR UZBEKISTAN
latest.abstract: Tourism statistics in many emerging destinations use the general consumer price index (CPI) to deflate tourism aggregates, although the expenditure structure of visitors differs substantially from the household consumption basket. This paper proposes a tourism price index (TPI) for Uzbekistan, with weights derived directly from inbound tourism consumption recorded in the Tourism Satellite Account (TSA) and price components based on the monthly CPI subindices and transport tariff indices already published by the national statistical office. The index is therefore constructed on the same conceptual basis as the tourism macroeconomic accounts and requires no additional price surveys. Over 2021–2025, the TPI increased by 59.8%, while the CPI increased by 46.2%. The real TPI reached 109.3, indicating that tourism goods and services became 9.3% more expensive relative to the general price level. Accommodation and food services, which account for 40.1% of inbound tourism consumption, contributed 35.0 percentage points, or 58% of total tourism price growth. Deflating inbound tourism consumption using the CPI overestimates its real growth over 2021–2024 by approximately 9% (5.64-fold versus 5.19-fold). Regional variants indicate that tourism price growth varies 3.7 times more across regions than consumer price growth. The results are robust to alternative weighting schemes. The proposed index can be compiled monthly at negligible additional cost and is recommended for inclusion in regular official statistics.

latest.title: Same hierarchy, different weights: a cross-national conjoint analysis of packaging cue evaluation across collectivistic and individualistic consumer contexts
latest.venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how extrinsic packaging cues, namely material, colour and logo placement, are evaluated by consumers in culturally contrasting national contexts, drawing on cue utilization theory (CUT) and Hofstede's individualism–collectivism dimension. Framing packaging as a multi-cue branding medium, the study examines how consumers hierarchically weight functional and symbolic cues under conditions of limited information. Design/methodology/approach A two-stage quantitative design was adopted. Stage 1 employed expert judgement (n = 27) to identify packaging attribute levels. Stage 2 deployed a choice-based conjoint experiment across two nationally contrasting samples: India (n = 278; collectivistic orientation) and Spain (n = 295; individualistic orientation). The resulting choice data were analysed using conditional logit models in R. Findings A consistent cue hierarchy emerged across both national contexts: material dominates in both, though bootstrapped confidence intervals reveal a two-tier structure in India, where colour and logo placement are not statistically distinguishable, compared to a fully confirmed three-tier hierarchy in Spain. Whilst the hierarchy's order is invariant, its internal weighting varies meaningfully across national contexts. In the Spanish country context, material dominates more strongly, consistent with analytic processing associated with individualistic orientations. In the Indian country context, logo placement carries comparatively greater weight, consistent with the social signalling function of brand identity in collectivistic national contexts. Originality/value This study extends CUT by addressing a question the theory has not previously resolved, namely what determines not merely which cues are diagnostic, but h

latest.title: Analisis Faktor-Faktor Kinerja Keuangan terhadap Kontribusi Pajak Penghasilan Badan pada Perusahaan Sektor Pertambangan yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2021–2025
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini menguji apakah profitabilitas, leverage, ukuran perusahaan, pertumbuhan penjualan, dan intensitas modal berkaitan dengan kontribusi pajak penghasilan badan perusahaan pertambangan yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) pada 2021–2025, yang diukur dengan cash effective tax rate (CETR). Sebanyak 22 perusahaan dipilih melalui purposive sampling, dan keluaran regresi yang dipakai untuk menguji hipotesis memuat 75 observasi dari laporan keuangan tahunan. Pengolahan data dilakukan dengan SPSS 25 melalui statistik deskriptif, uji asumsi klasik, regresi linear berganda, uji t, uji F, dan koefisien determinasi. Profitabilitas berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap CETR (t = 8.972,304; Sig. 0,000). Leverage (Sig. 0,611), ukuran perusahaan (Sig. 0,374), pertumbuhan penjualan (Sig. 0,488), dan intensitas modal (Sig. 0,292) tidak berpengaruh signifikan secara parsial; arah koefisien sesuai dugaan hanya pada leverage dan intensitas modal. Secara simultan kelima variabel signifikan (F = 17.972.763,389; Sig. 0,000). Koefisien determinasi sebesar 1,000 menandakan kecocokan model yang nyaris sempurna sehingga perlu ditafsirkan hati-hati dan diperiksa kembali dengan data mentah. Bagi praktik, hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa kemampuan menghasilkan laba merupakan ciri keuangan utama yang berkaitan dengan pajak kas yang dibayar pada sektor ini.

latest.title: Analisis Pengaruh Kualitas Produk dan Kualitas Layanan terhadap Niat Beli Ulang Konsumen pada UD. Rama Vasya
latest.abstract: Fluctuations in the number of purchases, inconsistent product quality, and suboptimal service when the store is busy are problems at UD Rama Vasya. This study aims to analyze the effects of product quality and service quality on consumer repurchase intention. The study employed a quantitative approach with an associative design involving 100 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires administered to consumers who met the study criteria and then analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS. The results showed that product quality had a positive regression coefficient of 0.112, but the coefficient was not statistically significant (p = 0.297). By contrast, service quality had a positive regression coefficient of 0.230 and was statistically significant (p = 0.033). These findings indicate that service quality is significantly associated with consumer repurchase intention in the context studied, whereas the relationship between product quality and repurchase intention was not supported by statistically significant evidence. The findings can inform managers at UD Rama Vasya in prioritizing improvements in service quality, particularly when the store is busy, to support consumer repurchase intention.

latest.title: What shared responses reveal about audience behavior: neural prediction and the emerging potential of peripheral synchrony
latest.abstract: Predicting audience responses to dynamic media remains a significant challenge in neuromarketing and neuroforecasting. Intersubject correlation (ISC) has been proposed to address this need by quantifying the temporal similarity of neural, physiological, and behavioral responses among individuals exposed to the same stimulus. This narrative mini-review examines how ISC relates to preferences, judgments, and behavior and proposes a conceptual framework for interpreting its predictive value. Across modalities, ISC consistently reflects shared stimulus processing and is associated with attention, alongside additional links to engagement, memory, and higher-order narrative processing. Neural ISC has shown associations with individual, group, and population-level outcomes, although findings vary by neural modality, analytic approach, and behavioral endpoint. Peripheral ISC derived from gaze, heart rate, electrodermal activity, and facial expressions provides complementary information about interindividual alignment, but direct evidence for predicting consumer outcomes remains limited. At the same time, neural and peripheral measures capture various aspects of shared response dynamics, and combining them in a multimodal ISC approach may help distinguish synchronization in different functional domains, including perceptual, attentional, autonomic, affective, and valuation-related processes, and clarify their relationship to the target outcome. The proposed framework therefore conceptualizes ISC as a probabilistic predictor whose predictive value depends on which functional processes underlie the observed synchrony and their relevance to the specific outcome of interest.

latest.title: Pengaruh Ulasan Pelanggan Online dan Persepsi Harga terhadap Niat Beli Konsumen Sudut Kedai di Metland Transyogi
latest.abstract: A sharp increase in menu prices at Sudut Kedai, coupled with shifting customer engagement online, raises a fundamental question: do online reviews and price perception actually influence purchase intention? This study examines both factors among Sudut Kedai consumers in Metland Transyogi. Questionnaires were distributed to 120 respondents who had read online reviews of Sudut Kedai, selected through convenience sampling. Data analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3.0. Online customer reviews demonstrate a positive and significant effect on purchase intention (path coefficient 0.245; T-statistic 3.271; p 0.001), as does price perception (path coefficient 0.373; T-statistic 4.861; p 0.000), with an R-Square of 0.220. Credible and informative reviews build buyer trust; prices perceived as proportional to quality enhance purchase intention. Sudut Kedai needs to actively manage customer reviews and maintain fair pricing to strengthen purchase intention amid an increasingly competitive culinary market.

latest.title: Analisis Perilaku Konsumen dalam Pengambilan Keputusan Pembelian pada Platform E-commerce
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Analisis Perilaku Konsumen dalam Pengambilan Keputusan Pembelian pada Platform E-commerce Khayatul Izah Program Studi Manajemen Fakultas Ekonomi dan bisnis Universitas Pamulang Jl. Surya Kencana No. 1, Pamulang Barat, Kec. Pamulang, Kota Tangerang Selatan, Banten 15417 Email: khayatulizah07@gmail.com ABSTRAK Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis perilaku konsumen dalam mengambil keputusan pembelian pada platform e-commerce. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan data yang dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner terbuka daring kepada 9 responden yang berpengalaman berbelanja melalui e-commerce. Data dianalisis melalui kondensasi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan, serta dilengkapi penghitungan frekuensi jawaban. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa harga murah, diskon, dan fleksibilitas waktu menjadi alasan responden berbelanja daring. Ulasan produk dinilai penting oleh 8 dari 9 responden, dan rating tinggi menjadi dasar yang paling banyak dipakai untuk memilih produk. Pembelian dilakukan karena kebutuhan (6 responden) maupun keinginan memberi penghargaan kepada diri sendiri (3 responden). Delapan responden pernah membatalkan pembelian, paling banyak karena ulasan buruk atau produk tidak sesuai, dan seluruh responden menyatakan bahwa belanja daring memengaruhi kondisi keuangan mereka, antara lain membuat lebih boros. Konsumen perlu mempertimbangkan kebutuhan dan kemampuan keuangan sebelum membeli, sedangkan penjual perlu menjaga kesesuaian produk dengan deskripsinya. Kata kunci: perilaku konsumen, keputusan pembelian, e-commerce, ulasan produk, perilaku konsumtif. ABSTRACT This study aims to analyze consumer behavior in making purchase decisions on e-commerce platforms. It employs a descriptive qualitative approach, with data collected through an online open

latest.title: Movement-Based Sleep Estimation Using a Smart Mattress: Adaptation of Cole–Kripke Algorithm and Comparison with a Multimodal Wearable
latest.abstract: Multimodal consumer wearables such as Garmin smartwatches combine movement with physiological signals to estimate sleep, whereas bed-based sensing largely relies on movement alone. How far movement alone, sensed from the bed, can go in estimating sleep is unclear. We adapted the Cole–Kripke algorithm to the movement signal of a WhizPad, a smart mattress with a 30-zone pressure array, using the original coefficients and one device-specific scale factor. Estimates were compared with those of a Garmin smartwatch, a proprietary comparator rather than a reference standard, across 28 paired nights in four participants. Epoch-level agreement between the two systems was high for sleep (98.08%) but substantially poorer for wake (30.76%; Cohen’s κ = 0.346). Over each system’s own sleep period, pooled wake after sleep onset (WASO) was 7.3 min lower for the WhizPad and pooled total sleep time (TST) 37.2 min higher, largely through a longer sleep period. The mattress registers bed entry, which Garmin does not export, allowing an exploratory, device-derived estimate of sleep latency that was not independently validated. These findings are descriptive and exploratory, and agreement does not establish the accuracy of either system as no polysomnography (PSG) reference was used. Physiological sensing in the bed and, ultimately, PSG validation are directions for future work.

latest.title: Greening Consumer Behavior in Bangladesh: Unraveling the Influence of Environmental Attitude and Social Media Marketing on Green Purchase Intentions
latest.venue: Asian Journal of Economics Business and Accounting
latest.abstract: Background: Green purchase intention in Bangladesh may be associated with social media communication, environmental attitudes, product knowledge and consumers' perceived capacity to make sustainable choices. Objective: This study examined the direct associations of social media marketing, environmental attitude, green product knowledge and perceived behavioural control with green purchase intention, together with the mediating role of product knowledge and the moderating role of perceived behavioural control. Methods: An online, self-administered questionnaire yielded 345 responses, of which 300 were retained for analysis. Participants were selected through purposive sampling. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to examine the proposed relationships. Results: Social media marketing (β = 0.372, p < 0.001), environmental attitude (β = 0.137, p <0.05), green product knowledge (β = 0.177, p <0.01) and perceived behavioural control (β = 0.124, p <0.05) were positively associated with green purchase intention. Green product knowledge partially mediated the associations of social media marketing (indirect β = 0.045, p <0.05) and environmental attitude (indirect β = 0.032, p <0.05) with purchase intention. Perceived behavioural control also moderated the social media marketing–purchase intention association (β = 0.100, p <0.05). The model explained 28% of the variance in green purchase intention. Conclusion: The findings suggest that informative digital promotion, environmental attitudes, product knowledge and perceived purchasing control are relevant to green purchase intentions among the surveyed Bangladeshi consumers. The cross-sectional design does not establish causality.

latest.title: Analisis Permintaan Konsumen terhadap Produk Makanan dan Minuman di Kalangan Mahasiswa
latest.venue: Neo Journal of economy and social humanities
latest.abstract: Consumer demand for food and beverage products among university students is an economic phenomenon influenced by various factors, both economic and non-economic. As a consumer group, students possess distinct characteristics that shape their consumption choices—most notably regarding budget constraints, price levels, income or pocket money, personal tastes, product quality, and the influence of their social environment. In microeconomic theory, consumer demand reflects the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity that consumers are willing to purchase, assuming all other factors remain constant (ceteris paribus) (Mankiw, 2021). This article aims to analyze the factors influencing the demand for food and beverage products among university students and to explain how economic considerations and consumer preferences shape purchasing decisions. The analysis focuses on variables such as price, pocket money, personal tastes, product quality, promotions, and the students' lifestyles. Theoretically, changes in price and purchasing power can affect the quantity demanded, while consumer preferences and perceptions help determine which products are ultimately consumed (Kotler et al., 2022). This study employs a qualitative approach—utilizing in-depth interviews, observation, and thematic analysis—to explore student consumption behavior, preferences, and the underlying considerations that drive demand. The findings offer insight into student consumption patterns and can serve as a guide for businesses in setting prices, enhancing product quality, and developing marketing strategies that align with the needs and purchasing power of university students.

latest.title: Social fashion identity: definition, scale development and empirical validation
latest.venue: Journal of Fashion Marketing and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose This study contributes to the conceptualization and measurement of how consumers use fashion to express multiple social identities. It aims to conceptualize social fashion identity, develop and validate its measurement scale and establish its dimensionality, reliability, convergent, discriminant and nomological validity. Design/methodology/approach Across two studies, social fashion identity is conceptualized, and a scale was developed and validated in a step-by-step process following Churchill (1979) and DeVellis (1991) procedures. Study 1 focused on construct conceptualization, item generation and scale validation, whereas Study 2 examined the nomological validity. Findings This paper validated the social fashion identity scale as a reliable two-dimensional construct consisting of fashion identity expression and fashion-based group belongingness. Social fashion identity was distinct from fashion consciousness and product involvement, positively associated with fashion consciousness, and positively related to consumers' willingness to pay more for fashion items. Practical implications The social fashion identity scale offers fashion companies a tool to segment their clients, enabling more personalized customer experiences within the fashion market. Furthermore, the findings can contribute to the effectiveness of fashion brands' product development, marketing and pricing strategies by providing a deeper understanding of social influences on consumer behavior. Originality/value This research introduces the novel construct and its measurement. Social fashion identity explains the capacity to select, coordinate and adapt clothing and accessories to express personal identity while signaling affiliation with social groups, thereby reflecting the dynamic interplay bet

Beyond Personalization: The Paradox of Trust, Consumer Autonomy and Engagement in AI-Driven Interactive Digital Media
latest.venue: Journal of Art Design and Creative Media
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed digital and interactive media by enabling personalized content, algorithmic recommendations and increasingly responsive consumer experiences. Although these developments offer opportunities to improve relevance, convenience and engagement, they also raise important questions concerning privacy, consumer autonomy and trust. Existing discussions frequently emphasize the benefits of personalization and the effectiveness of digital engagement, yet these perspectives may overlook the possibility that the same technological features that enhance consumer experiences can also generate perceptions of surveillance, manipulation and loss of control. This conceptual article examines the dual nature of AI-driven interactive digital media through an integration of the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, Privacy Calculus Theory and Psychological Reactance Theory. The article proposes a conceptual framework in which personalization, perceived interactivity and algorithmic transparency influence consumer responses through two interconnected pathways: a value-creation pathway associated with perceived relevance, trust and engagement, and a resistance pathway associated with privacy concerns, perceived manipulation and psychological reactance. Consumer autonomy is further considered as an important boundary condition shaping these relationships. The proposed framework contributes to digital marketing and interactive media scholarship by conceptualizing consumer engagement as a conditional outcome rather than an inherently positive consequence of technological sophistication. The article also offers implications for digital marketers, platform designers and policymakers seeking to develop more transparent, trustworthy and consumer-centred dig

latest.title: AI-Enabled Hospitality Services and Consumer Repurchase Intention: The Roles of Technology Readiness, Technological Empowerment, Emotional Attachment, and Trust
latest.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
latest.abstract: This study investigates how technology adoption propensity (TAP) is associated with consumers’ intention to repurchase AI-enabled hospitality services by examining the mediating roles of perceived technological empowerment (PTE) and brand emotional attachment (BEA), as well as the moderating role of trust in AI (TAI). Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework and the technology readiness perspective, cross-sectional survey data were collected from 439 guests of deluxe hotels in Greater Cairo, Egypt, and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that TAP is positively associated with both PTE and BEA. PTE is positively associated with BEA and partially mediates the TAP–BEA association, and the sequential indirect association between TAP and repurchase intention through PTE and BEA is significant. BEA emerges as a strong predictor of repurchase intention, while TAI strengthens the relationship between BEA and repurchase intention. The study contributes by showing that a general technology predisposition is linked to post-adoption repurchase intentions through a cognitive-to-affective chain (empowerment, then brand attachment) while retaining a larger direct link to attachment, and by identifying trust in AI as a boundary condition of the attachment–intention link. Because the design is cross-sectional and measures intentions, the results indicate associations rather than causal effects.

latest.title: Determinasi Brand Evangelism Hasil Personalisasi, Influencer–Brand Fit, Dan Perceived Authenticity Melalui Consumer Trust
latest.abstract: The emergence of social media as a marketing tool has transformed consumer behavior toward brands. This study aims to analyze the effects of personalization level, influencer–brand fit, and perceived authenticity on brand evangelism, with consumer trust as a mediating variable. This study employs a quantitative approach through a survey of 268 social media users selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with the SmartPLS software. The results show that personalization level, perceived authenticity, and consumer trust have a positive effect on brand evangelism. In addition, personalization level, influencer–brand fit, and perceived authenticity have a positive effect on consumer trust. However, influencer–brand fit does not have a significant direct effect on brand evangelism. These findings underscore the importance of personalization, authenticity, and consumer trust in driving brand evangelism on social media.

latest.title: Amul’s European expansion – the Spanish dilemma
latest.abstract: Learning outcomes At the end of the case discussion, students will be able to: Case overview/synopsis Jayen Mehta, Managing Director of Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation, faced a critical strategic choice as the company prepared for its first major international expansion into Europe. After launching Amul milk products in the USA in March 2024, the company looked to expand its international presence. Spain’s sizable dairy market, its cooperative experience and its potential connection to the larger European market made it a possible entry point to the wider European market. However, the challenges were significant, including stringent regulations, competition from mature European dairy companies, evolving consumer tastes and preferences and the rise of plant-based products. Mehta was thus faced with the question of whether Spain should be Amul’s first European market and, if so, how the company should enter the market to achieve the cooperative’s long-term international goals while managing risk and allocating resources effectively. The case depicts how a farmer-owned cooperative from an emerging economy seeks to transfer its domestic strengths, cooperative capabilities and brand heritage to a developed market. Complexity academic level This case is designed for undergraduate and postgraduate students, as part of their course in international business, international marketing and strategic management. It is especially appropriate for sections that focus on Global Marketing Management, International Market Entry Strategies and Internationalisation of Firms, Global Strategy, Emerging Market Multinational Enterprises and International Entrepreneurship. Subject code CSS 5: International Business.

latest.title: THE INFLUENCE OF DIGITAL MARKETING ON CONSUMER PURCHASING DECISIONS.
authors: Caroline Dias da Silva de Carvalho
latest.abstract: This article aimed to analyze the impact of digital marketing and digital influencers on consumer behavior. The methodology used comprised the following research methods: in the first phase, a bibliographic review was conducted in order to analyze, in the scientific literature, the transformation from traditional marketing to digital marketing, as well as the role of social media and digital influencers in purchase decisions; in the second stage, a field research was carried out through the application of a structured questionnaire, aiming to identify consumers' perceptions regarding the influence exerted by these agents on their consumption habits. The results obtained indicated that digital marketing significantly influenced consumer behavior, making consumers more active and informed, while digital influencers exerted a strong impact on opinion formation and purchase decisions, especially due to the credibility and identification established with the audience. It was concluded that digital marketing and digital influencers played an essential role in contemporary business strategies, being fundamental for building relationships with consumers and strengthening brands in the digital environment.

latest.title: The Influence Of Supervision And Work Discipline On Improving Employee Performance (Survey Of The Sales Team At CV Hana Prima Lestari Tasikmalaya City)
latest.venue: Jurnal Ekonomi Islam Akuntansi dan Manajemen
latest.abstract: A decline in employee performance within the sales team at CV Hana Prima Lestari indicates issues with the team's work performance, likely stemming from suboptimal supervision and low levels of employee discipline. This study aims to determine the impact of supervision and work discipline on improving the performance of the CV Hana Prima Lestari sales team, both individually (partially) and collectively (simultaneously). A quantitative approach using a causal-associative method was employed. Data were collected via questionnaires distributed to 63 sales team respondents at CV Hana Prima Lestari. Data analysis techniques included validity testing, reliability testing, classical assumption testing, multiple linear regression analysis, partial testing (t-test), and simultaneous testing (F-test) using SPSS version 25 software. The results indicate that supervision has a positive and significant partial effect on employee performance. Work discipline was also found to have a positive and significant effect on employee performance. Simultaneously, supervision and work discipline were shown to have a significant combined effect on employee performance. These findings suggest that stricter supervision and higher levels of discipline lead to optimal improvements in employee work performance. In conclusion, the performance of the CV Hana Prima Lestari sales team can be enhanced through supervision and work discipline.

latest.title: The Impact of Sustainability Labels on Consumer Purchase Intentions and Buying Behaviour
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: As the world of business moves at a fast pace towards a greener future, sustainability has transformed from being a mere marketing trend to a vital core strategic policy in the world of business. This paper explores the impact of sustainability labelling on purchase behaviour of the consumer amongst a targeted group of 100 Gen-Z and Young Adult respondents. Using a quantitative research methodology, primary data is collected with a structured digital survey via Google forms and analysed with percentage analysis. The research scope is defined on assessing the response of Gen Z consumer in general retail markets, meeting the 4 major objectives of this research. The impacts of eco labelling influence on purchasing decisions, the role of consumer awareness and trust in purchase decision, the effect of pricing premiums and product quality and the attitude-behaviour gap that does not transition to action at point of purchase. Empirically, our data suggests that though 82.0% of the respondents do show some form of searching for sustainability labels, and 71.0% have some moderate-strong influences towards the labels in making their final purchase, there is still a lot of scepticism and pricing barriers. Where 46.0% suggests that a high price difference, compared to other products, is the main reason for going back to normal alternatives. Ultimately, the findings offer actionable insights for businesses to bridge this gap of intention vs behaviour, genuine brand trust, and push for sustainable growth of the market.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
hot.abstract: Abstract Chatbots are now able to engage in sophisticated conversations with consumers in the domain of relationships, providing a potential coping solution to widescale societal loneliness. Behavioral research provides little insight into whether these applications (apps) are effective at alleviating loneliness. We address this question by focusing on “artificial intelligence (AI) companions”: apps designed to provide consumers with synthetic interaction partners. Study 1 examines user reviews of AI companion apps and finds correlational evidence suggesting that these apps help alleviate loneliness. Study 2 finds that AI companions successfully alleviate loneliness on par only with interacting with another person and more than other activities such as watching YouTube videos. Moreover, consumers underestimate the degree to which AI companions improve their loneliness. Study 3 uses a longitudinal design and finds that an AI companion consistently provides momentary reductions in loneliness after use over the course of a week. Study 4 provides evidence that both the chatbots’ performance and, especially, whether it makes users feel heard, explain reductions in loneliness. Study 5 provides an additional robustness check for the loneliness-alleviating benefits of AI companions and shows that self-disclosure and distraction alone do not explain AI companions’ effectiveness.

hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Abstract Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Impact of digital transformation on SME’s marketing performance: role of social media and market turbulence
hot.abstract: Despite the rising relevance of digital transformation, there is still a knowledge vacuum due to limited literature available on digital transformation. This study aims to examine the impact of digital transformation on the marketing performance of small and medium enterprises. This research seeks to fill this void by adopting the technology adoption model in order to explore how in a fast-changing technological environment, digital transformation plays its role in firm specific capabilities that are imperative for a firm to adopt, and how they impact firm’s marketing performance. Combination of convenience sampling as well as snowball sampling was used to collect the data. Utilizing survey data from 316 small to medium-sized enterprises in the twin cities (Islamabad & Rawalpindi), Pakistan the results indicate that digital transformation has a positive influence on small and medium enterprises’ marketing performance. This encourages businesses to take advantage of the opportunity presented by new digital technologies and industry-wide digitalization trends by adopting new technologies and improving their digital capabilities in order to increase their productivity, efficiency, and innovation as well as their marketing performance. Hence this study is a practical demonstration of how developing digital transformation may be used to develop novel digital products and services and thereby improve marketing performance that leads to the overall corporate performance. Finally, the study contributes to the literature by evaluating the proposed model that describes the relationships between digital transformation, social media marketing, market turbulence and marketing performance concurrently.

hot.title: Supply Chain Resilience: A Critical Review of Risk Mitigation, Robust Optimisation, and Technological Solutions and Future Research Directions
hot.venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management
hot.abstract: Abstract This study systematically evaluates the literature of supply chain resilience by integrating bibliometric and network analysis techniques. This analysis is conducted following the dynamic capability, as a theoretical lens, to understand and analyse supply chain resilience. We extracted and curated 294 peer‐reviewed articles from leading academic databases, Web of Science and Scopus, covering the period from January 2000 to 2024. We applied two complementary network analysis methods, a keyword co‐occurrence network (KCON) to analyse the frequency and interrelationships among key terms, and a research focus parallelship network (RFPN) to map the connectivity among research streams. These analytical approaches revealed three distinct research clusters, optimisation for supply chain resilience, technology adoption for supply chain resilience, and resilience strategies against disruptions and risk management. By linking emerging trends in digital transformation with traditional risk management practices, this study offers a new perspective for both academic inquiry and managerial practice. Practically, integrating digital technologies, especially digital twin and machine learning, into risk management processes offers a strategic roadmap for real-time monitoring and decision-making in supply chain resilience. Furthermore, this study identifies significant research gaps, including an exploration of micro‐level dynamics within organisations, and the development of advanced simulation techniques and robust approaches to manage uncertainties.

hot.title: Organizational culture, digital transformation, and product innovation
hot.abstract: This research fills a knowledge gap by introducing a new conceptualization of digital transformation through a multidimensional digital transforming capability. It further examines the influence of four cultural types on this capability and its subsequent impact on product innovation . Empirical findings reveal that adhocracy, followed in descending order of influence by clan, market, and hierarchy cultures, is positively related to digital transforming capability, which in turn is positively related to product innovation in terms of new product newness, meaningfulness, and performance. Additionally, new product newness and meaningfulness each positively mediate the effect of digital transforming capability on new product performance.

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: Theory and theory development: Guidelines for establishing theoretical gaps, foundations, contributions, and implications
hot.abstract: Theory guides the acquisition and advancement of knowledge. Despite its importance, developing and refining theories remains a formidable task, given the inadequate clarity, inherent confusion, and compounding complexity faced by scholars in theory development. In response, this article offers clear, coherent, and constructive guidelines to tackle these challenges in theory development. Adopting the 3 E s involving the author’s expertise , experience , and exposure , this guide offers a sequential approach to addressing theoretical gaps , theoretical foundations , theoretical contributions , and theoretical implications . This all-inclusive, accessible, and actionable resource seeks to benefit a diverse range of stakeholders, including both emerging and established scholars, which, in turn, contributes to ensuring the effective development of theories and, by extension, the return on value of these theories for funders, institutions, and, most importantly, the target beneficiaries (e.g., consumers, firms, society at large) of well-developed, theory-informed research.

hot.title: Lower Artificial Intelligence Literacy Predicts Greater AI Receptivity
hot.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms society, understanding factors that influence AI receptivity is increasingly important. The current research investigates which types of consumers have greater AI receptivity. Contrary to expectations revealed in four surveys, cross-country data and six additional studies find that people with lower AI literacy are typically more receptive to AI. This lower literacy–greater receptivity link is not explained by differences in perceptions of AI's capability, ethicality, or feared impact on humanity. Instead, this link occurs because people with lower AI literacy are more likely to perceive AI as magical and experience feelings of awe in the face of AI's execution of tasks that seem to require uniquely human attributes. In line with this theorizing, the lower literacy–higher receptivity link is mediated by perceptions of AI as magical and is moderated among tasks not assumed to require distinctly human attributes. These findings suggest that companies may benefit from shifting their marketing efforts and product development toward consumers with lower AI literacy. In addition, efforts to demystify AI may inadvertently reduce its appeal.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs : An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other. Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: What you see is not what you get: ESG scores and greenwashing risk
hot.abstract: This paper shows that ESG scores capture a company’s greenwashing behavior. Greenwashing accusations are most prevalent among large companies with high ESG scores. We empirically employ a novel theoretical model that distinguishes between the communication of a company’s environmental efforts (apparent environmental performance) and its actual environmental impact (real environmental performance). The correlation of the apparent (real) environmental performance with ESG scores is significantly positive (negative). Therefore, ESG scores are unsuitable for measuring real environmental impact. Thus, investors focusing on high ESG-rated companies may unknowingly increase their greenwashing risk exposure, and academics may use misleading information to assess greenwashing risk. • ESG scores are positively correlated with greenwashing cases. • ESG scores mainly measure the apparent rather than the real environmental performance. • Higher analyst coverage limits the exaggeration of apparent environmental performance.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: The impact of digital HRM system and digital transformation on HR efficiency with organizational agility as a moderator
hot.abstract: The study focuses on understanding the moderation effect of organizational agility in the impact of digital HRM system and digital transformation on HR efficiency in organizations intending to excel in the digital era. This study examines the association between digital HRM systems, digital transformation, and HR efficiency, considering the moderating role of organizational agility. Based on the study model, the authors proposed five hypotheses to be tested in this study. They adapted the study instrument based on quantitative descriptive approach and distributed 500 questioners to collect 385 responses. The study’s findings reveal that both digital HRM systems and digital transformation impact HR efficiency. The significant findings were that digital HRM systems (β = 0.456, p < 0.001) and digital transformation (β = 0.194, p = 0.006) have a positive and significant impact on HR efficiency. In addition, organizational agility serves as a moderator in the relationship between digital HRM systems and HR efficiency (β = 0.154, p = 0.025) but has no effect on the relationship with digital transformation (β = − 0.075, p = 0.248). This study contributes to the literature by demonstrating the role of digital HRM systems and digital transformation as key organizational resources that enhance HR efficiency. It also highlights how organizational agility and digital capabilities serve as dynamic resources, contributing to an organization’s adaptability and sustained competitive advantage. The future research directions and limitations are presented at the end.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The past, present, and future of sustainability marketing: How did we get here and where might we go?
hot.abstract: The ever-increasing concerns about global sustainability have sparked intense debates and actions across various sectors, with marketing playing a pivotal role in influencing both the problem and potential solutions. This article maps the historical trajectory of sustainability marketing, analyzes current trends, and explores future directions to enhance sustainability within marketing practice. We show that sustainability marketing has historically centered on resource conservation and green marketing , but in recent years its scope has expanded to encompass a broader range of topics. These include the circular economy , anti-consumption, regulatory frameworks, innovation, carbon emissions , as well as the social and ethical considerations inherent in sustainability marketing. We propose three main areas within which sustainability marketing might expand in the future: system-driven changes, business-driven changes, and consumer-driven changes. Our analysis aims to deepen the understanding of sustainability marketing and inspire marketers to explore questions and solutions that will contribute to a sustainable future.

hot.title: Greenwashing and market value of firms: An empirical study
hot.abstract: In today's business environment, green or sustainable claims are rising as companies strive to strengthen environmental practices in response to climate change and sustainable development challenges. However, with increasing expectations of sustainable performance, companies encounter mounting financial pressure to adopt more efficient sustainable practices, which may lead some to exploit sustainability efforts for their own gain. Many companies make environmentally friendly assertions to conceal or mask their actual activities—a phenomenon known as greenwashing—which fosters public scepticism about the authenticity of their green messaging. This study employs an event study methodology to examine how the stock market values greenwashing news, drawing on 121 global greenwashing news since the 2015 Paris Agreement. Our findings reveal a negative correlation between greenwashing news and stock market reactions. The market reactions to greenwashing news are more negative for firms with greater ESG performance than for weak ESG performance. Additionally, greenwashing news supported by concrete evidence elicits stronger adverse reactions. Companies operating in the manufacturing industry experience more significant market value losses than those in the service sector. The findings also indicate that the Asia-Pacific market demonstrates particularly strong negative responses to greenwashing news compared to other stock markets. This study contributes to the signalling theory and advances the literature on corporate sustainability practices by providing empirical insights in a global context.

hot.title: Digital literacy, digital accessibility, human capital, and entrepreneurial resilience: a case for dynamic business ecosystems
hot.abstract: This study examines the role of digital literacy, digital accessibility, and human capital in fostering entrepreneurial resilience among entrepreneurs in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). These countries serve as exemplary models in digital transformation, particularly in navigating crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Grounded in the resource-based view and the theory of dynamic capabilities, this research investigates how these factors contribute to entrepreneurial resilience. This study employs structural equation modeling to analyze survey data from 317 individuals with entrepreneurial experience. According to the findings, digital literacy, accessibility, and human capital significantly enhance innovation, strengthening entrepreneurial resilience. Agility is identified as a key moderator, amplifying the positive impact of these competencies on resilience. Although the success of entrepreneurial ecosystems has often been attributed to entrepreneurial actors, resource providers, connectors, or entrepreneurial intentions, this study underscores the importance of fostering digital competencies and agility to build resilient entrepreneurial ecosystems. It offers policymakers and business leaders insights into the mechanisms that enhance resilience in dynamic and crisis-affected environments where the digital landscape is rapidly evolving.

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising.
